title: Observation Bandwidth, Reobservation, and Causal Order
author: Ingolf Lohmann

active_hypotheses.claim: For the registered finite-bandwidth transition generator, observation at or above the registered boundary reduces missed-transition and aliasing error relative to sub-boundary polling.
active_hypotheses.null_hypothesis: After phase, load, jitter, duty-cycle, and event-count controls, the above-bound conditions do not improve missed-transition rate by at least 0.10 absolute compared with the strongest sub-boundary condition.
active_hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: The above-bound conditions improve missed-transition rate by at least 0.10 absolute and the direction survives all registered controls.
active_hypotheses.decision_rule: Support requires an absolute missed-transition-rate reduction >= 0.10 and a two-sided 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the reduction whose lower bound is > 0 across the registered phase and jitter strata.
active_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Reject the registered policy claim if the margin is not reached, if the confidence interval includes 0, or if the effect disappears in any preregistered phase or jitter stratum.
not_claimed: universal applicability to arbitrary event streams

active_hypotheses.claim: Post-effect reobservation reduces false completion classifications relative to transport-acknowledgement-only classification under the registered fault model.
active_hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Reobservation does not reduce false completion rate by at least 0.05 absolute relative to transport acknowledgement alone.
active_hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: Reobservation reduces false completion rate by at least 0.05 absolute without unequal authority or hidden intervention information.
active_hypotheses.decision_rule: Support requires an absolute false-completion-rate reduction >= 0.05 with a two-sided 95% confidence interval whose lower bound is > 0 and no increase in false-hold rate greater than 0.05 absolute.
active_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Reject if the error reduction margin is not reached, the interval includes 0, false holds exceed the registered bound, or unequal information explains the result.

active_hypotheses.claim: Explicit predecessor bindings reconstruct intervention-defined causal graphs more accurately than timestamp order under the registered clock and network perturbations.
active_hypotheses.null_hypothesis: With equal admissible information, explicit predecessor bindings do not improve macro-F1 by at least 0.10 over timestamp-order reconstruction.
active_hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: With equal admissible information, explicit predecessor bindings improve macro-F1 by at least 0.10 and maintain edge-direction validity under all registered perturbations.
active_hypotheses.decision_rule: Support requires mean macro-F1 improvement >= 0.10 and a cluster-bootstrap 95% confidence interval by graph whose lower bound is > 0.
active_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Reject if the margin is not reached, if a cycle is introduced in more than 1% of trials, or if the advantage depends on metadata unavailable to the baseline.
not_claimed: complete causal discovery from observational data

active_hypotheses.claim: Observer-relative receive-order inversion can occur while one intervention-defined causal graph remains invariant.
active_hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Under the registered controls, receive-order inversion necessarily changes the reconstructed causal graph.
active_hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: At least 95% of registered receive-order-inversion trials preserve the intervention-defined graph when explicit predecessor evidence is available.
active_hypotheses.decision_rule: Support requires graph invariance >= 0.95 with a one-sided 95% confidence lower bound >= 0.90.
active_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Reject if the confidence lower bound is < 0.90 or if graph preservation requires hidden or post hoc edges.

active_hypotheses.claim: In two independently instrumented physical apparatuses, explicit causal-order features add reproducible out-of-sample predictive information beyond timestamp-only features for registered postconditions.
active_hypotheses.null_hypothesis: The causal-feature model improves held-out log loss by less than 0.01 or fails replication in either apparatus.
active_hypotheses.alternative_hypothesis: The causal-feature model improves held-out log loss by at least 0.01 in each apparatus with a bootstrap 95% confidence interval excluding 0.
active_hypotheses.decision_rule: Support requires timestamp-only minus causal-feature held-out log loss >= 0.01 in each apparatus and a bootstrap 95% interval whose lower bound is > 0 in each apparatus.
active_hypotheses.falsification_condition: Reject if either apparatus misses the margin, either interval includes 0, leakage is detected, or the result fails the frozen replication analysis.

blocked_claims.reason: No registered measurement currently distinguishes this identity from weaker predictive, representational, or existing-physics alternatives.
